name: lua
title: Lua 5.4 (ANSI C, with its own test suite)
_doc: Not a game and not here to be one. Lua is strict ANSI C with no platform layer at all, and it ships THIRTY-FOUR files of its own tests -- which makes it an ORACLE in the same role as c-testsuite and Csmith rather than another target: the tests are built on assert(), so running them under PRISM and reaching the end is the check.
_units: Every .c except luac.c and onelua.c. luac.c is the bytecode compiler and has a main() of its own; onelua.c is Lua's single-file amalgamation, which #includes every other unit -- listing it alongside them defined all 155 public functions twice, which is precisely what the duplicate-symbol report is for and what it said on the first build.
_defines: LUA_USE_C89 keeps it to what PRISM's tier-0 already promises. The default build reaches for POSIX (dlopen for require, popen, locale) through LUA_USE_LINUX; C89 is Lua's own switch for a host without those, which is exactly this one.
